thread:
eng-oncall-bot: Pager: high error rate and streaming disconnects for enterprise tenant AcmeCorp (dedicated pool acmecorp-dc-west1). Symptoms: 504s from gateway, websocket closes, client retries. Escalating to L2.

sre-cheng: I'm taking. Can someone paste last 10m of proxy logs and pool health?

support-ryan: Acme support ticket shows repeated client timeouts at ~15:11 UTC. They see streaming sessions cut at ~30s mark and then a spike of reconnects. Link: https://acme.example/status (customer link redacted)

infra-mike: running quick pool check now. `redwoodctl pools status --tenant acmecorp --region dc-west1`

infra-mike: results -> replica count 4, CPU healthy but GPU responder queue length spiking to 500-1200 for the last 8m. KV cache hit rate dropped to 12%. Could be head-of-line due to many stalled streams.

sre-cheng: grabbing proxy logs. here's a sample of the gateway upstream errors: ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T15:12:07Z","tenant":"acmecorp","upstream":"acme-gw","error":"upstream_reset","http_code":504,"path":"/v1/stream"}
{"ts":"2026-03-15T15:12:09Z","tenant":"acmecorp","upstream":"acme-gw","error":"connection_closed","http_code":502,"path":"/v1/stream"}
```

networking-ana: On the networking side, we see an unusual number of half-closed TCP sessions from Acme's gateway IP block (10.12.0.0/20). Their gateway may be retrying aggressively on websocket close.

cust-ops-jane: Confirmed with Acme SRE: they rolled a change to their app gateway at 15:00 UTC that reduced idle timeout from 2m -> 30s and enabled aggressive retry (backoff 200ms, max 5). They deployed to prod only for a subset of services but maybe the streaming route got affected.

sre-cheng: That matches. Short idle time + aggressive retry will produce reconnect storms; for streaming we get stuck KV caches and long queue times -> 504s. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Ask Acme to revert gateway change or increase idle timeout, 2) Apply temporary rate limiting on ingress for acmecorp, 3) Scale dedicated pool replicas, 4) Route streaming traffic to stateless fallback model variant.

pm-lena: Customer impact: several Acme endpoints degraded (internal dashboards, live-collab). SLA impact likely for last 18m. Need comms if we keep mitigation >30m.

infra-mike: I'm going to scale pool to reduce queue pressure. Executing `redwoodctl scale --pool acmecorp-dc-west1 --replicas 8` now.

eng-oncall-bot: Action logged: infra-mike scaled acmecorp-dc-west1 from 4 -> 8 replicas.

sre-cheng: While scaling completes (estimate ~3m), enable transient rate limit to damp reconnect storms: `redwoodctl routes update --tenant acmecorp --route /v1/stream --rate-limit 100rps --burst 200 --duration 15m`

networking-ana: Applied rate limit. Monitoring for drop in queue length.

support-ryan: I just messaged Acme SRE and asked them to revert the gateway idle timeout or increase to >=90s and to add jitter on retries. They replied: "rolling back in 5m to test".

sre-cheng: Also applying a route fallback so new connections can be served by a stateless streaming variant that doesn't rely on large KV caches: ```yaml
route: /v1/stream
fallback_model: llama-3-7b-stateless-v1
condition: tenant == "acmecorp" and streaming == true
```

eng-oncall-bot: Route fallback applied by sre-cheng. Canary: 10% traffic.

cust-ops-jane: Acme confirmed rollback done at 15:20. They report steady decreases in reconnects.

infra-mike: Pool replicas finished scaling. Queue length dropped to ~80-120, KV cache hit back to 67%. Latency improved.

sre-cheng: Observed 504s drop from ~18/min -> 1/min over 6m. Streaming sessions reestablished normally. Marking mitigation effective.

pm-lena: Handing off to infra-mike for 1h watch window and to prepare RCA. SRE follow-up to author postmortem for customer-facing summary.

infra-mike: I'm on watch. Will keep the rate-limit for 30m and canary fallback route at 10% for 1h. If stable, will remove scaling back to baseline (4) in ~90m.

sre-cheng: Notes for RCA: root cause appears to be customer gateway change (idle timeout + aggressive retry) causing reconnect storms + head-of-line blocking in dedicated pool due to long-lived streaming sessions and stateful KV dependencies. Contributing factor: our default attacker-protection/backpressure didn't dynamically throttle streaming reconnects per-tenant early enough.

support-ryan: Logged case update for Acme. Proposed customer-facing blurb: "We observed transient streaming disruptions caused by interaction between your gateway idle/retry settings and our streaming routing; we mitigated by applying temporary rate-limits, scaling your dedicated pool, and enabling a stateless fallback to restore sessions. Please revert the idle timeout change or add retry jitter. Our eng team will follow with next steps."

pm-lena: +1. I'll draft a short status update for Acme and CSM.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident timeline summary created and attached to ticket RED-INC-2026-045.

infra-mike: After 50m watch: metrics stable. Removing route rate-limit now and scaling pool down to 4 replicas in a staged manner: `redwoodctl scale --pool acmecorp-dc-west1 --replicas 6` -> wait -> `--replicas 4`.

eng-oncall-bot: Action logged: infra-mike scaled acmecorp-dc-west1 8 -> 6.

eng-oncall-bot: Action logged: infra-mike scaled acmecorp-dc-west1 6 -> 4.

networking-ana: Verified TCP session histogram returned to pre-incident shape. No lingering half-closed sessions.

sre-cheng: Closing incident thread for now. Postmortem owners: SRE: cheng, Infra: mike, DevEx: ryan. Action items: (1) Add tenant-level streaming backpressure rule to auto-throttle reconnect bursts, (2) Add detection alert when KV cache hit drops >40% for a tenant, (3) Update runbook to suggest explicit gateway idle timeout recommendations for enterprise customers (90s+ and retry jitter).

pm-lena: Will coordinate comms and legal-safe customer message.

cust-ops-jane: Thx all — Acme SRE said incident is resolved on their end, will monitor. They appreciated quick mitigations. :thumbsup:

eng-oncall-bot: Thread closed by sre-cheng at 15:56 UTC.

sre-cheng: I'll split these notes into the postmortem doc and link the customer-friendly summary. If anything new shows up ping me and I'll reopen.
